correctness.rationale: For all n>=1 and real a, shift reflection reduces negative a to nonnegative. Disjoint residue supports yield (n+1)c_n^2/2 <=3/8; a=0 yields <=3/4. Overlapping integer shifts k<=n/2 obey the central-mass F_m induction, strictly outside n=2,k=1 (checked exactly as 9/16). For k>n/2 and n>=20 the exact binomial ratio products imply p_n(j)<=c_n exp(-d(j)^2/n), and the modal diameter-one property yields max mass <3c_n/4, hence K M^2<27/32. For all n<=19 and k in [1,n], 190 exhaustive exact-integer comparisons across 3990 positions complete the finite bridge. Every coefficient and normalization is defined; an independent auditor has not assessed the argument.

originality.rationale: Li (2026) explicitly identifies H_0<=2H_infinity for all fair weighted Bernoulli sums as Conjecture 1.1; Theorem 1.4 proves coefficient 2 for positive Rényi orders alpha>=1/2 but not alpha=0, while Theorem 1.5 has a larger variable coefficient at the endpoint. Jain--Sah--Sawhney (2021) prove weaker support-versus-concentration estimates. This claim resolves the exact endpoint for an infinite all-real-parameter weight family but does not purport to resolve the general conjecture. Targeted indexed-record and web searches did not locate a covering theorem. Unindexed equivalents remain possible.

value.rationale: The parent 2026 paper states a sharp open endpoint Rényi-entropy conjecture relevant to subset-sum collisions and randomized bin packing. Equal weights plus one arbitrary outlier form the first natural defect family from the binomial extremizer, with an infinite discrete/continuous collision transition at integral weights. The result rigorously settles the conjectured exponent for every size and real outlier, rather than a single parameter slice; the exponent remains genuinely sharp as n tends to infinity. The finite 190-case bridge is motivated by the universal Gaussian localization cutoff. It does not resolve the unrestricted conjecture.
